current_answer: Jev is TypeSafe AI's hosted model for bounded Choice, Score and Noul judgments; your code must check each answer and own the action, review and fallback. TypeSafe lists jev-1.13.0 at $0.042 per million input tokens with free output; signups reopened on 27 September 2026 but new users currently get no free credit. OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify and Opper serve it at the same or rounded list price, while lookalike reseller storefronts charged 3–16× that price. Open projects and 46 creator videos show Jev in email sorting, ticket triage, moderation, model routing, trading gates and games, but no audited project or company claim has been independently verified as a production deployment. TypeSafe documents 17 limitations, including arithmetic, dates and long irrelevant context. Independent open-weight alternatives (Kev, CLM, Laya) and runtimes such as Ollaya exist; none has verified parity with Jev.

summary: Jev answers from a fixed answer set: Choice (up to 255 options), Score (up to 10 levels), Noul (probability of yes). It does not generate text and accepts text input only.
Signups reopened on 27 Sep 2026 (CEO post); free credit for new users is temporarily disabled. The earlier $5 credit rests on secondary reports with a conflicting first-hand report.

List price $0.042/M input, output free on TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Cloudflare and (in its models API) Vercel; Opper and Vercel's web page round to $0.04; Netlify bills credits. Lookalike resellers displayed 3–16× the list price.
Cost per decision depends on counted input tokens; third parties report a fixed overhead of roughly 250–300 tokens even for one-line requests.
The official Python package is typesafe-sdk 0.7.2 (not typesafe-ai); the SDK retries 408, 429 and 5xx with a 30 s budget. There is no 250 ms TypeSafe default timeout.
Choice confidence matches (n·p_max − 1)/(n − 1) in TypeSafe's examples; it is not the probability of being correct. The Score formula is undocumented.
46 creator videos show Jev running on concrete tasks in 13 use-case groups; start times are the creators' chapter markers, not watched by the pool.
Seven company and analyst production or cost claims are listed; none is independently verified.
uncertainty: No pool-made Jev call, account, bill or signup; the console returned HTTP 403. Live status codes and limits are third-party reports.
Whether question text, criteria and failed requests are billed is undocumented; Jev Router billing and failure behaviour are undocumented.
Score confidence for 4+ levels is unknown; independent calibration tests each use one dataset.
No video frames or transcripts were viewed.
Reddit, X, TikTok, Lobsters and GitHub code search could not be read in the daily scan.
Search analytics and Search Console data were unavailable; pages were chosen from qualitative signals.
